result:
Solution A is very likely wrong. It claims that isomorphic conjugacy quandles force isoclinism, so no counterexample exists. But the problem asks for the minimum order of such a counterexample, which presupposes one exists. A's answer of 0 contradicts the problem's premise. Its argument is also only asserted, with no verification.

Solution B gives a positive integer and states that counterexamples first appear at order 64. It gives no construction or proof, so I can't verify it. I have a vague recollection of the literature on isoclinism and conjugation quandles pointing to a smaller order, possibly 32, which would mean B is also incorrect. I can't confirm either value from memory.

Even so, B is the more plausible of the two. Its claim is at least consistent with the problem's premise, while A's is not.

WINNER: B
